author: Unsigned statement (corpus lists General Conference of SDA)
work: Fundamental Principles of Seventh-day Adventists, 1889 Year Book, p. 150, Principle XIX
text: XIX. That the Spirit of God was promised to manifest itself in the church through certain gifts, enumerated especially in 1 Corinthians 12 and Ephesians 4; that these gifts are not designed to supersede, or take the place of, the Bible, which is sufficient to make us wise unto salvation, any more than the Bible can take the place of the Holy Spirit; that, in specifying the various channels of its operation, that Spirit has simply made provision for its own existence and presence with the people of God to the end of time, …
note: Principle XIX: the gifts are “not designed to supersede, or take the place of, the Bible,” and the Spirit provides for its presence through them “to the end of time”; the statement names no individual.

author: Ellen G. White
work: A Sketch of the Christian Experience and Views of Ellen G. White (1851)
text: I recommend to you, dear reader, the word of God as the rule of your faith and practice. By that Word we are to be judged. God has, in that Word, promised to give visions in the “last days;” not for a new rule of faith, but for the comfort of his people, and to correct those who err from Bible truth.
note: EGW, 1851: the word of God is “the rule of your faith and practice”; visions are “not for a new rule of faith” but for comfort and “to correct those who err from Bible truth.”

author: James White (signed “JAMES WHITE.” at ARSH February 14,  1856, page 158.6)
work: Note appended to “From Bro. Bingham,” Advent Review and Sabbath Herald, February 14, 1856 (reprinted in “Note to Bro. Barr,” January 22, 1857, page 96.7)
text: It is well known that we have been charged with testing all men by the visions, and of making them the rule of our faith. This is a bold untruth, of which those who uttered it were not ignorant. … I still say that the Bible is my rule of faith and practice, and in saying this, I do not reject the Holy Spirit in its diversities of operations. … I believe them to be the property of the church, and a test to those who believe them from Heaven.
note: James White, 1856: the charge of “testing all men by the visions, and of making them the rule of our faith” is “a bold untruth”; “the Bible is my rule of faith and practice”; the visions are “a test to those who believe them from Heaven.”

author: James White
text: The gift of prophecy is by the apostle classed with the callings of the Christian church in Ephesians 4:11-13. … These were all given at the same time, all for the same purpose, all to cease at the same time. … Will those continue till the church is perfected, ready to meet her descending Lord? So will the gift of prophecy.
note: James White, 1868: prophets were given with evangelists, pastors and teachers, “all to cease at the same time,” so the gift of prophecy continues “till the church is perfected, ready to meet her descending Lord.”

author: Uriah Smith
work: Replies to Elder Canright’s Attacks on Seventh-day Adventists (1887)
text: But these Scriptures make provision for the operation of the Holy Spirit, not only in ordinary, but in extraordinary methods in the church to the end of time. These latter are explicitly enumerated in 1 Corinthians 12 and Ephesians 4. … Prophecies of their especial revival in the last days, are numerous. See Joel 2:28; Acts 2:17; 1 Corinthians 1:7; Revelation 12:17; etc. … But what was given in this way would not constitute another Bible nor an addition to the Bible.
note: Uriah Smith, 1887: the gifts of 1 Corinthians 12 and Ephesians 4 operate “to the end of time,” with a last-days revival (Joel 2:28; Revelation 12:17), but what is given “would not constitute another Bible nor an addition to the Bible.”

author: Ellen G. White
work: “An open letter from Mrs. E. G. White to all who love the blessed hope,” Review and Herald, January 20, 1903 (letter text: 17LtMs, Lt 196, 1902, par. 5)
text: The Lord has sent his people much instruction, line upon line, precept upon precept, here a little, and there a little. Little heed is given to the Bible, and the Lord has given a lesser light to lead men and women to the greater light. O, how much good would be accomplished if the books containing this light were read with a determination to carry out the principles they contain!
note: EGW, 1903: because “Little heed is given to the Bible,” the Lord “has given a lesser light to lead men and women to the greater light.”

author: J. N. Loughborough
work: The Great Second Advent Movement: Its Rise and Progress (1905)
text: We are in the very period of time when a people were to arise who would keep all the commandments, and who would also “have the testimony of Jesus” … —the “spirit of prophecy.” … That during the last sixty years such a people have arisen, bearing just such a message, among whom the gift of prophecy has been manifested. … These writings have never placed themselves above the Bible, but they do constantly exhort to the most careful study of the word of God, pointing to it as the great standard by which our cases will be examined in the final judgment.
note: Loughborough, 1905: reads Revelation 12:17 with 19:10 (“the testimony of Jesus” — “the spirit of prophecy”) of the people raised since 1844, and says Ellen White’s writings “have never placed themselves above the Bible.”
